passages.provision_quote: In an action against a defendant who developed, modified, or used artificial intelligence that is alleged to have caused a harm to the plaintiff, it shall not be a defense, and the defendant may not assert, that the artificial intelligence autonomously caused the harm to the plaintiff.
passages.note: Chaptered bill bars an AI developer/user from escaping liability by claiming the AI acted autonomously, holding them legally responsible when their system causes harm.

rows.reasoning: AB 316, which Krell authored and which was signed into law, removes the defense that 'the artificial intelligence autonomously caused the harm to the plaintiff' for any defendant who developed, modified, or used the AI. This operative clause holds AI developers legally responsible when their systems cause harm, matching rung 3 and excluding the lighter rungs (no interference, voluntary guidelines) and the heavier rungs (mandatory pre-deployment testing or approval), which the bill does not impose.
